The emulator has no evidenced audit continuity mechanism for power events. A snapshot collected while node-1 runs does not establish log preservation during power loss. The required plan, storage guarantees, and power-event validation are missing.

No complete password inventory or approved generation record establishes at least 112 random bits under the referenced Key Management Annex. Password length alone would not prove generation entropy. The authentication-service alternative in GD-27 must remain available rather than requiring both branches.

The evidence does not record testing and application of all applicable critical patches under policy and CP constraints. An image version is not a patch-governance history. Supply the policy, advisories, compatibility tests, and installation records.

No local patch-installation policy is included. The model cannot infer an organization's required timing and process from container versions. That policy is a prerequisite to checking compliant installations.

No TEMPEST assessment or mitigation evidence is supplied. Packet filtering and encryption order do not establish emanations protection. The physical deployment and applicable TEMPEST requirements need an external assessment.

The export inventories logical devices and image identities, not an AO-approved hardware inventory. Physical equipment identities, serial numbers, and approval records are missing. Logical graph counts do not discharge those requirements.

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: Lean checks the retained MSC data topology. Full-export totals remain optional diagnostics and are not required premises or review acceptance criteria. The finite graph checks do not establish drawing completeness, physical fidelity, or the full documentation requirement.
entries.model_claim: The retained MSC projection has 23 devices and 24 data cables. Imported device IDs are unique and declared cable endpoints are valid. Optional administration workstations, management-only switches, and management links do not determine the retained counts.

entries.reason: No per-network-domain authentication service is established as the selected Objective alternative to GD-21. Device-to-device IPsec authentication is not that administrator authentication service. Selecting the alternative requires its domain separation, account policy, and service evidence.

No confirmed-incident and reporting-event history establishes notification within 24 hours to the required JIMS/NSA recipients. The timing obligation is conditional on an incident and needs both event timestamps and delivery evidence. Absence of a recorded incident in a short snapshot is not a proof of the reporting process.

No incident report is supplied for checking registration details, contacts, classification, component identities, timestamps, description, remediation, and requested assistance. A probe log is not the specified report. Each required field and its accuracy need evidence when the reporting condition occurs.

No workflow connects a confirmed security-function failure to the required report. Detecting a modeled forwarding failure would only identify a possible trigger. The incident classification and actual reporting action need separate evidence.

The model has no classified-information compromise/spillage event semantics or reporting history. A cross-level blocking proof does not establish reporting if such an event occurs. The event definition, detection record, and required notification are missing.

No incident process classifies and reports malicious traffic entering or leaving Gray. A firewall counter alone neither identifies malicious activity nor proves notification. The classification rule must also retain the presumption described in N-48.

The snapshot supplies no incident records showing whether any unauthorized device or user gained access to the classified network via the solution, or whether the Solution Owner reported that evidence. The trigger does not require demonstrated access to classified information. Packet peer labels do not establish detection and reporting of every such incident. Authorization, detection, and reporting records are required for triggered cases.

The evidence does not establish whether any Solution Component sent traffic with an unauthorized destination address or whether the Solution Owner reported such an incident. The trigger covers traffic without a classified-payload restriction, including control traffic. A model rejection theorem establishes one prevention mechanism but does not prove the required incident response. Destination authorization and reporting records are required for triggered cases.

No configuration-change audit trail identifies malicious changes and their required reports. A pinned configuration provides a baseline but does not identify who changed it or why. Change attribution, incident classification, and reporting records are required.

The network model contains no privilege-escalation event or corresponding report. Device roles do not describe human/process privilege transitions. An identity and privilege audit plus reporting evidence is needed.

Certificate observations can help look for duplicate credential use, but the current model does not detect the specified multi-IP VPN condition or establish that it was reported. A certificate/session correlation rule and an incident workflow are needed. Finding no duplicate in one sample would not prove the reporting obligation.

No tamper sensors, physical inspection results, or incident reports are supplied. A virtual topology cannot establish detection and reporting of physical tampering. Physical evidence and reporting records are required.

The flow model describes fail-closed behavior under selected readiness assumptions, but does not establish the required report when either actual encryption layer fails to protect data. Such a proof needs an event-to-report workflow as well as detection of the protection failure. The prevention theorem alone is insufficient.

No operational record shows reporting of the specified service degradation. The explicit exclusion for Black-network connectivity must remain in the incident predicate; an ordinary underlay outage cannot automatically be counted as a reportable MSC security incident under this row. Cause classification and reporting records are needed.

The snapshot does not define the expected outer connection count over time or classify discrepancies as malicious. A single SA count cannot prove reporting of malicious discrepancies. The expected-count policy, monitoring history, and report evidence are missing.

The snapshot does not establish an expected inner connection count or reports for malicious deviations. Separate inner and outer counts need their own event conditions. Monitoring and classification records are required before checking the inner reporting obligation.

No personnel clearance roster or classification assignment is supplied. The explicit Black-administrator exception must be retained when assigning required clearance levels. Network role names cannot prove the relevant human clearance or exception.

The model does not identify the humans acting as Security Administrators and Auditors. Distinct account or container names would not prove that those roles are held by different people. A personnel-role assignment and enforcement record is required.
No information-assurance training records are supplied for the required personnel. Successful use of the emulator is not evidence of completed training. Dated training and role records are needed.

MSC-RB-4 delegates its obligation to the CSfC Key Management Requirements Annex. The local row contains no replacement predicate and the destination annex was not supplied. Relocation is not withdrawal or evidence that the requirement is optional; obtain the applicable destination text before assessing node-1.

The snapshot has no authoritative assignment of separate human administrators to Red and Gray domains. That personnel obligation is independent of the excluded AW containers, so neither their original separation nor their assumed absence proves it. Identity, role, and access records would be needed for a whole-solution personnel assessment. The protected-data theorem has no administrator-separation premise.

No periodic physical inspection records are included. A graph imported once cannot prove recurring inspections of the deployed equipment. The schedule, inspection results, and responsible personnel must be documented.

MSC-RB-7 delegates its obligation to the CSfC Continuous Monitoring Annex. The local row contains no replacement predicate and the destination annex was not supplied. Relocation is not withdrawal or evidence that the requirement is optional; obtain the applicable destination text before assessing node-1.

No disposal events or preceding certificate-revocation/CAK-destruction actions are modeled. The IPsec profile uses the certificate branch; the CAK branch applies only when selected. A lifecycle proof needs dated revocation and disposal records with the required ordering.

MSC-RB-9 delegates its obligation to the CSfC Key Management Requirements Annex. The local row contains no replacement predicate and the destination annex was not supplied. MSC-RB-10 delegates its obligation to the CSfC Symmetric Key Management Requirements Annex. The local row contains no replacement predicate and the destination annex was not supplied. Relocation is not withdrawal or evidence that the requirement is optional; obtain the applicable destination text before assessing node-1.

The optional mandatory access-control role-policy arrangement is not established in node-1. Device firewall rules are not evidence of separation of human roles through that mechanism. If selected, the policy and its enforcement must be audited separately.

The saved 273 probes and Lean model proofs exercise selected emulator properties, but the mandatory MSC Testing Annex was not supplied. They therefore cannot establish completion of every annex test or maintenance of all required artifacts. Obtain the annex, map every applicable test, execute missing tests, and retain the specified results.

entries.reason: The imported S1 and S2 labels are unordered and must represent the complete classification/compartment/dissemination tuple. Physical source authentication, arbitrary spoofing, all runtime behaviors, and actual classification assignments remain outside the established conclusion.
entries.model_claim: The execution-based theorem quantifies over arbitrary IPv4 headers, messages, and finite paths. A source host whose source address belongs to its Red subnet can deliver through the observed route/filter/XFRM and virtual-link model only to a Red host with the same complete security label. Finite checks establish source restrictions on inner-to-Red outputs, their transfer to host inputs, and disjoint cross-level address ranges. Generic induction preserves those restrictions and the original source header. The older authorized-host-pair pipeline also retains its narrower conditional theorems.
entries.title: Meaning of security level

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: Concrete checks cover every retained interface pair, possible IPsec tag, compatible outgoing selector, observed SA owner, and trust-domain relationship. Generic provenance and stack induction lift those checks to arbitrary finite executions, including loops. The seal operation denotes trusted authenticated IPsec encryption. Cryptographic secrecy, implementation independence, physical appliance independence, fragmentation, dynamic state changes, and a complete refinement of Linux behavior remain separate obligations.
entries.model_claim: A clear Red-origin datagram that reaches Black through any admitted finite execution is exactly the original datagram sealed by an observed inner SA and then by an observed outer SA. The layer witnesses identify different logical appliances, distinct declared trust domains, and complete admitted peer sessions. The exact order follows from filter/selector compatibility and a reusable stack invariant. Observed virtual links and OVS switching supply the execution graph.
entries.title: Two independent nested tunnels

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: The stages are derived from actual admitted steps in the snapshot model. A two-wrapper packet using two outer SAs fails the ordered-stack condition. The statements concern protected Red payloads in fixed sampled IPv4 state under trusted IPsec operations; they do not assert encryption of visible routing headers or control packets.
entries.model_claim: For a clear tracked Red-origin message, every reachable Gray packet has exactly one observed inner seal around the original datagram. Every reachable Black packet has an observed outer seal around that inner seal. The original header and message are preserved inside the wrappers. Approved control traffic retains its explicit exception.
entries.title: Red, Gray and Black data

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: Symmetric declarations and sampled SAs are supplemented by typed runtime correspondence, observed route selection, supported packet-processing semantics, and credential/session admission checks. Missing lists remain distinct from observed empty lists, and extra interfaces or policies cannot disappear behind intended records. Positive traces establish nonempty admitted executions for selected data and IKE headers. The observations were collected sequentially; an atomic capture, future service availability, all application protocols, and complete Linux/strongSwan conformance remain outside the claim.
entries.model_claim: Every imported tunnel record has a matching reversed record, and all sampled encryptors report established tunnels. Eight endpoint records describe four peer pairs in the selected IPsec/IPsec instance. Full architectural pair coverage and protocol correctness are separate obligations. Additional finite checks compare all retained live interfaces, peer attachments, static routes, routing-rule shapes, forwarding flags, XFRM policies/states, and switch ports with the declared profile. Four checked 19-step ICMP-shaped data traces cover both directions at both security levels, remove both layers, and pass the destination host's INPUT policy. A proved runner lemma turns each successful computation into an execution of the safety relation.
entries.title: Site-to-site tunnel structure

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: Lean checks a complete dedicated mapping for the four representative Red hosts and four inner encryptors. Each host has a connected inner with the same site and security level. All Red cables at that host reach its assigned inner, and all Red cables at that inner reach only its owning host. Every declared inner has an owner. The importer rejects missing or ambiguous attachments before deriving peer authorization. The representative-host abstraction and logical container separation do not establish physically independent certified components. Outer sharing is permitted rather than required; separate deployed outers do not violate the permission.
entries.model_claim: Each declared Red host has one exclusive, connected inner in its site and security level. Every declared inner is covered by the host mapping. The finite topology checks support per-Red logical component ownership for the current four-host profile. They do not establish physical independence or prohibit permitted outer sharing. Each Red host and its assigned inner also declare the same parsed Red subnet.
entries.title: One inner component per Red network

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: Lean checks distinct declared trust domains and their sampled public CA identifiers. Each local and declared peer identity is bound to the observed certificate inventory, including issuer and authority-key metadata. Equal trust domains agree on sampled CA identities; different trust domains have distinct reported CA key identifiers. The checks do not prove signature validity, private-key independence, absence of cross-signing, exhaustive credential stores, or actual rejection of unauthorized peers. Management infrastructure is optional and excluded; MACsec CAK clauses are inactive.
entries.model_claim: The retained inner security levels use distinct declared trust labels and distinct sampled public CA key identifiers. Complete local/peer/CA inventories bind those observations to all eight declared encryptor endpoints. Matching sampled metadata is a bounded observation claim, not a cryptographic validation result.
entries.title: Cryptographic security-level separation

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: The flow theorems reject cross-level transmission and delivery for every modeled state and packet, and permit authorized same-level delivery under readiness assumptions. They do not promise unconditional delivery during failures, infer real identities from packet addresses, or prove computational secrecy. Shared infrastructure is allowed by this architectural statement, although separate physical-component requirements still apply elsewhere.
entries.model_claim: Cross-level and unauthorized modeled traffic is blocked for every readiness state. An authorized same-level packet transmits and is delivered when the specified sender/receiver readiness assumptions hold. The latter is a conditional model result, not unconditional network availability.
entries.title: No inter-level Red communication

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: Lean proves that every nonempty declared Gray interface address parses and that all numeric Gray addresses are distinct across interfaces, sites, and levels. The stronger global uniqueness check covers the address-assignment clause. Outer selectors are also tied to the declared inner peer endpoints, and forwarding contracts restrict the modeled FORWARD subset. Address attribution, complete packet-class/control exceptions, and Linux fidelity remain separate obligations.
entries.model_claim: The imported addressed Gray interfaces have valid, globally distinct numeric IPv4 addresses. Tunnel-derived outer selectors bind the intended inner peers, and accepted modeled outer traffic satisfies the corresponding address/direction/protocol contract.
entries.title: Gray address assignment and intended peers

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: The Gray cut proof establishes that all imported virtual Gray walks between differently labeled inner components encounter a removed Gray Firewall. It covers arbitrary finite path lengths. Physical realization and graph completeness remain premises; the source does not impose a same-level firewall waypoint.
entries.model_claim: Every imported Gray path joining differently labeled inner components includes a Gray Firewall, as established by removing those firewalls and proving no bypass walk remains. The induction covers all finite walks. Same-level paths need no universal waypoint under this statement.
entries.title: All cross-level Gray paths are filtered

entries.disposition: Conditional service branch not exercised in the selected projection
entries.reason: The AW grouping and filtering clauses are outside the experiment. No online local Gray CA service is declared in the projection, so its conditional grouping is not exercised. Loaded trust anchors do not establish a hosted CA service. Introducing a local CA would require an authoritative classification ordering and path analysis; absent AWs create no gap now.
entries.title: Gray management grouped with highest level

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: Outer forwarding rules have independent policy guards, and all retained local filter chains use explicit peer or control-service contracts. Credential admission checks bind sampled SAs to permitted peer sessions. Execution-based protection and isolation supply the retained processing consequences. Organization approval of the selected controls, complete implementation fidelity, fragmented packets, and future state remain separate boundaries.
entries.model_claim: The imported outer encryptors have their own guarded FORWARD tables, and the symbolic authorization relation blocks cross-level and unauthorized Red transmission. The existence of Gray Firewalls is not used as a substitute for those outer rules. Complete outer interface filtering remains outside the checked contribution.
entries.title: Outer filtering is additional to Gray firewalls

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: The untrusted-Black placement and bounded FORWARD policy now have proofs. Shared-host containers do not establish physical separation, no product listing is supplied, and INPUT/OUTPUT plus the complete approved control set remain outside the model. SR-12 retains its narrower Public Internet trigger.
entries.model_claim: Removing Outer Firewall vertices from the retained Red/Gray/Black cable graph disconnects every outer encryptor from BLACK for all finite walks. Each outer also has a checked two-edge path through an Outer Firewall in the original graph, so the cut does not rely on disconnection. The bounded FORWARD allowlist is checked at every Outer Firewall. The full-route theorem explicitly identifies an Outer Firewall among the visited vertices of each outer-to-Black route.

Node-1's simulated Black network is not identified as the Public Internet. A selected Internet design needs an authoritative resolution; the table must not silently erase the prose or make TRANSEC universally mandatory.
entries.title: Outer TRANSEC in prose

entries.reason: The export does not establish ownership/control, trusted-third-party status, or facility protection at the highest connected classification. It also does not assign a highest classification to S1/S2. The stated exception for the Outer Firewall must be retained when obtaining the required physical evidence.
entries.title: Gray ownership and physical protection

entries.reason: No classification authority has determined whether Gray metadata is itself classified. The applicability limitation concerns that additional Gray information, not the intended singly encrypted Red payload. entries.title: MACsec must retain end-to-end inner protection

entries.reason: The symbolic flow requires independent inner and outer peer-authenticated flags and blocks transmission when either flag is false. Intended configurations select public-key authentication at both IPsec layers. The theorem assumes the flags correctly summarize IKE, certificate, and trust checks; it does not prove those checks or the unselected MACsec handshake.

The NSA-approved KGS condition applies to selected CAK/CKN generation, which is absent here. A complete IPsec certificate policy and annex-based credential audit are still required.
entries.title: Device certificates and symmetric-key generation

Its absence does not violate a permission, and a PSK-only replacement would not satisfy the separate required certificate authentication. Selecting the augmentation would require the Symmetric Key Management Annex and matching IKE evidence.
entries.title: Optional IPsec preshared-key augmentation

entries.reason: The profile consistently uses IPv4, which is allowed by the independent address-family choices. The permission does not require simultaneous IPv4 and IPv6 support. No IPv6 implementation theorem is claimed by the current IPv4 model.
entries.title: IPv4/IPv6 independence

entries.reason: The snapshot contains specific control allowances, including Black underlay OSPF on routers and IKE on gateways. The organization/AO-approved control policy is missing, and the model does not cover all local control traffic or multicast handling. A proof must retain necessary Layer 2 control and explicit approvals rather than treat every non-data packet as forbidden.

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: Observed routes and XFRM state connect outer forwarding to the selected encryption operation. Captured namespace processes and startup evidence support the no-routing-daemon check for outer encryptors; OSPF belongs to BLACK and the separate Outer Firewalls. The retained complete-datagram execution model supplies routing and layer provenance. Unknown future programs, fragmented packets, actual source attribution, and full implementation conformance remain outside the current claim.

The no-routing-protocol clause is not proved by those theorems. OSPF on separate Black/Outer Firewall routers is not an outer-encryptor protocol.
entries.title: Outer routing restriction and encrypted forwarding

The approved Red service addresses and ports are not supplied, and the model does not prove full service-specific filtering.
